name: Yangyul Ju
bioIntro: I am a results-driven Polymer Engineering researcher specializing in complex fluid rheology and advanced multiphysics modeling. My research establishes critical structure-property-performance relationships across a diverse spectrum of advanced materials systems.

By bridging experimental complex fluid mechanics with multi-scale computational frameworks, I deliver targeted structural and interfacial engineering solutions across battery materials, dispersion systems, and soft matter.
bioHighlights: Silicon Anode Slurries for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Optimizing multi-component battery pastes to accommodate lithiation-induced volume expansion and ensure long-term cyclability.
SWCNT Dispersions: Tailoring dispersion kinetics and formulation to construct highly interconnected, resilient electrical and mechanical percolation networks.

Surface-Modified Separators for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Engineering functional coatings (e.g., GO-POSS) to accelerate Li+ transport kinetics, enhance thermal safety, and suppress lithium dendrite growth.
Hydrogels & Suspensions: Elucidating micro/nano-scale particle interactions, structural gelation recovery, and non-linear viscoelastic properties for diversified advanced polymer composites.

expertise.title: 1. COMSOL Multiphysics
bullets: Electro-chemo-mechanical coupling (diffusion-induced stress in silicon anodes)
Thermal management (heat transfer in heterogeneous composites)

expertise.title: 2. MATLAB Programming
bullets: Electrical percolation modeling to validate experimental findings on interparticle interactions and network dynamics

expertise.title: 3. Rheology & Material Characterizations
bullets: Advanced Rheology (LAOS/SPP): Quantified non-linear viscoelasticity, shear deformation, and structural recovery mechanisms of silicon anode slurries, SWCNT dispersions, and composite hydrogels.
Electrochemical Diagnostics: Deconvoluted dynamic bulk, SEI, and charge-transfer resistance parameters across multi-component battery systems utilizing operational EIS, CV, and GITT setups.
Interfacial & Surface Science: Tuned binder chemistry and hybrid polymer composite coatings to suppress lithiation-induced volume expansion and mitigate lithium dendrite growth.
